### Historical audit — S0072

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is available here; the referenced images and other chunk were not inspected.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| **Goal** — line 22, `model_request`, chars [0,165818) | The instructed task was an editable single-photo indoor reconstruction. The student **inferred** a shipboard sleeping and machinery compartment; that interpretation is not independently verified. |
| **Build and source audit** — line 22 | The program constructed separate assets for architecture, bunks, lockers, chair, machinery, benches, wall fittings, pipes and lights. It specified colored finishes, not image textures. Supports and surfaces were grouped, with shared bunk dimensions and explicit floor-contact coordinates; those choices do not prove actual contact or correct pose. |
| **Input and adoption** — line 22 | A controller/user source-audit instruction was actually present in the student conversation. The subsequent program adopted duplicate-key and dimension checks, conditional World initialization, and named-subtree material copying; it also added a cabinet ledge support. This is evidence of receipt and code adoption, not independent confirmation that every check or connection is correct. No separate teacher diagnosis or proposed patch is visible in this chunk. |
| **Student exploration** — line 22 | After step 1, the student reported low column and bunk feet, low locker tops, and chair occlusion; it hypothesized camera pitch as one cause. The next program changed camera aim, room width, bunk levels and placement, partition, chair and machine. After step 2, it reported remaining local placement and brightness issues, hypothesized depth rather than lens error, and kept the camera fixed while moving furniture, adding an edge post, reducing exposure and changing floor roughness. These are student observations and hypotheses, not independently viewed image findings. Multiple simultaneous changes prevent attributing any improvement to one cause. |
| **Execution and selection** — line 22; line 20 `execution_result`, chars [0,31223); lines 24–25 | The embedded results report successful renders for steps 1 and 2. Step 3 independently reports `ok: true`, a completed 16-sample render, saved PNG and blend file, and empty stderr. The student replied `DONE`; the controller selected step 3. Line 23 records a completed read-only final review session with no tool calls. |

**Outcome:** Successful execution and selection are visible; **reconstruction correctness is unknown**, not formally verified. There is no visible functional regression result or independent geometric evaluation. The render logs establish many mesh objects, but not whether all intended semantic objects are visible, correctly connected, posed, textured, framed or lit. The student’s comments identify possible camera, occlusion, brightness and floor-seam issues; their resolution in the final image cannot be checked from this text.

**Transferable lesson:** Separate observed discrepancies from camera-versus-local hypotheses, and preserve composite dependencies when revising. Here, source-level checks and complete-asset moves were adopted, but concurrent camera, layout and lighting changes limit causal inference. **Task-specific uncertainty:** shipboard identity, furniture depths, cropping, actual contacts and final visual fidelity remain unresolved without the images and geometric checks.
